subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare the names 'Bharata' and 'India': who used each first, and what does each name come from?
prompt_hi: 'Bharata' aur 'India' naam compare karo: kisne pehle use kiya, aur har naam kahaan se aaya?
answer: Bharata was used by people of the land itself (linked to the Bharata clan in the Rig Veda and later texts); India was used by outsiders — Greeks, from 'Indos', from the river Sindhu.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Say the words of Article 1 of the Constitution about our country's name.
prompt_hi: Constitution ke Article 1 mein desh ke naam ke baare mein kya likha hai?
answer: 'India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.'

subject: sst
prompt_en: A student says: 'Bharat is the old name of a different country; India is the new country.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Ek student kehta hai: 'Bharat ek alag purane desh ka naam hai; India naya desh hai.' Kya galat hai?
answer: Both names refer to the same country; the Constitution says 'India, that is Bharat', so both are official names.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Chinese travellers like Xuanzang called the land 'Yindu'. Which earlier name does 'Yindu' sound closest to, and what does that suggest?
prompt_hi: Xuanzang jaise Chinese yatriyon ne is bhoomi ko 'Yindu' kaha. 'Yindu' kis puraane naam jaisa lagta hai, aur isse kya pata chalta hai?
answer: It sounds like 'Hindu'/'Indu', suggesting the Chinese name also came, directly or indirectly, from the river Sindhu.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Make a word-chain map of how 'Sindhu' became 'India': write each step and who said it.
prompt_hi: Ek word-chain banao ki 'Sindhu' kaise 'India' bana: har step aur kisne bola, likho.
answer: Sindhu (people of the land, Sanskrit) → Hindu (Persians) → Indos/Indus (Greeks) → India (later European usage).

subject: sst
prompt_en: A Purana describes Bharata as the land 'north of the ocean and south of the snowy mountains'. Why is this an interesting source for historians?
prompt_hi: Ek Purana mein Bharata ko 'samudra ke uttar aur barfeele pahadon ke dakshin' wali bhoomi kaha gaya hai. Historians ke liye yeh source dilchasp kyon hai?
answer: It shows that people long ago already thought of the whole land between the Himalayas and the seas as one region with one name.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Predict: if a traveller from a faraway land visited and heard about a great river first, what might they name the whole country after?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar door desh ka yatri aaye aur sabse pehle ek badi nadi ke baare mein sune, to woh poore desh ka naam kis cheez pe rakhega?
answer: After the river — just as outsiders named India after the Sindhu (Indus).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Does your town or city have more than one name (for example an old name and a new name, or a name in another language)? Say both and what one of them might tell us.
prompt_hi: Kya tumhare sheher ke ek se zyada naam hain (jaise purana aur naya, ya kisi aur bhasha mein)? Dono batao aur unme se ek kya batata hai.
answer: Any town with two names and a reasonable meaning clue, e.g. Prayagraj/Allahabad, Mumbai/Bombay, Chennai/Madras, Kolkata/Calcutta, Bengaluru/Bangalore; names often tell about a goddess, river, ruler or language.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Explain to a classmate why our country has two official names and where they come from.
prompt_hi: Ek classmate ko samjhao ki hamare desh ke do official naam kyon hain aur woh kahaan se aaye.
answer: Bharata is an old name from inside (linked to the Bharata clan in the Vedas and later texts); India comes from outsiders' word for the river Sindhu (Sindhu → Hindu → Indos → India); the Constitution keeps both: 'India, that is Bharat'.

subject: sst
prompt_en: What was the Great Bath, and in which city was it found?
prompt_hi: Great Bath kya tha aur kis sheher mein mila?
answer: A large, waterproofed brick tank with steps, found at Mohenjo-daro, probably used for special bathing or rituals.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why do covered drains along the streets suggest that Harappan cities were carefully planned?
prompt_hi: Galiyon ke saath dhakki naaliyan yeh kyon dikhaati hain ki Harappa ke sheher dhyaan se planned the?
answer: Drains had to be laid out before or along with houses and streets, connected and sloped, and kept clean — this needs planning and some shared rules or organisation.

subject: sst
prompt_en: At Lothal, archaeologists found a large brick basin linked to a channel, near the sea. What was it probably used for, and what does it tell us?
prompt_hi: Lothal mein samudra ke paas ek bada eent ka basin mila jo ek channel se juda tha. Iska shayad kya use tha, aur isse kya pata chalta hai?
answer: Probably a dockyard for boats; it tells us Harappans traded by water.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Has the Harappan script been deciphered (read) yet?
prompt_hi: Kya Harappan lipi abhi tak padhi (decipher) ja saki hai?
answer: No, it has not yet been deciphered.

subject: sst
prompt_en: A storybook says: 'One day a huge flood came and the Harappan civilisation vanished forever.' What is wrong with this?
prompt_hi: Ek kahani ki kitaab kehti hai: 'Ek din bahut badi baadh aayi aur Harappan sabhyata hamesha ke liye gayab ho gayi.' Isme kya galat hai?
answer: The decline was slow, over a long time, with several causes (climate change, rivers drying or shifting, less trade); people moved to smaller settlements and many skills and ways of life continued.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Predict: if a river that a city depended on slowly dried up, what would happen to farming, trade and the city over many years?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar jis nadi pe sheher nirbhar tha woh dheere-dheere sookh jaaye, to saalon mein kheti, vyapaar aur sheher ka kya hoga?
answer: Farming would fail, food would become scarce, trade would fall, and people would slowly leave for other places — the city would shrink.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare a Harappan city with a modern Indian city: name one thing that is similar and one that is different.
prompt_hi: Ek Harappan sheher ko aaj ke Bharatiya sheher se compare karo: ek cheez jo milti-julti hai aur ek jo alag hai.
answer: Similar: planned streets, drains, water storage, markets and trade, crafts. Different: modern cities have electricity, cars, concrete, a written language we can read; Harappan cities used baked bricks and no large palaces have been found.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Harappan weights were made in standard sizes. Why would traders need standard weights?
prompt_hi: Harappa mein baat (weights) ek jaise standard size ke bane the. Vyapaariyon ko standard weights ki zaroorat kyon thi?
answer: So that buying and selling was fair and everyone measured goods the same way across different cities.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Describe in words the map location of Dholavira and Lothal compared with Harappa and Mohenjo-daro.
prompt_hi: Map ke hisaab se shabdon mein batao ki Dholavira aur Lothal, Harappa aur Mohenjo-daro ke mukable kahaan hain.
answer: Dholavira and Lothal are to the south-east, in Gujarat near the coast (Kachchh and near the Gulf of Khambhat); Harappa and Mohenjo-daro are to the north-west, along the Indus river system in Pakistan.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Look at the drains and water supply on your street or colony. What would a Harappan engineer praise, and what would they suggest improving?
prompt_hi: Apni gali ya colony ki naaliyan aur paani ki vyavastha dekho. Ek Harappan engineer kis cheez ki tareef karta aur kya sudharne ko kehta?
answer: Any reasoned answer comparing covered/connected drains, sloping, cleaning and water storage with Harappan practice (e.g., praise covered drains; suggest covering open drains and storing rainwater like Dholavira).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Teach a younger child what the Harappan civilisation was and how we know about it without reading its writing.
prompt_hi: Ek chhote bachche ko sikhao ki Harappan sabhyata kya thi aur uski lipi padhe bina hum uske baare mein kaise jaante hain.
answer: A civilisation of planned cities (about 2600-1900 BCE) in the Indus and Ghaggar-Hakra valleys, with grid streets, drains, standard bricks and weights, crafts and trade; we know from archaeological remains — buildings, seals, beads, pots, tools — because the script is not yet read.

subject: sst
prompt_en: The Vedas were passed down by memory for centuries, yet stayed nearly unchanged. Why is that remarkable, and how was it done?
prompt_hi: Vedas sadiyon tak yaad karke aage badhaye gaye, phir bhi lagbhag badle nahi. Yeh kamaal kyon hai, aur yeh kaise hua?
answer: Long texts usually change when passed by word of mouth, but students learnt them with special recitation methods (repeating words in different patterns) and careful teachers, so errors were caught.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Where did the Buddha attain enlightenment and where did he give his first teaching?
prompt_hi: Buddha ko gyaan kahaan mila aur unhone pehla updesh kahaan diya?
answer: Enlightenment at Bodh Gaya (Bihar); first teaching at Sarnath (near Varanasi).

subject: sst
prompt_en: What did the Buddha call the way between too much luxury and too much hardship?
prompt_hi: Bahut zyada aaraam aur bahut zyada kasht ke beech ke raaste ko Buddha ne kya kaha?
answer: The Middle Path (Middle Way).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare the teachings of the Buddha and Mahavira: give one idea that is shared and one that is special to each.
prompt_hi: Buddha aur Mahavira ki seekhon ko compare karo: ek saanjhi baat aur har ek ki ek khaas baat batao.
answer: Shared: both lived about 2,500 years ago and taught non-harm and good conduct over rituals. Buddha: the Middle Path to end suffering. Mahavira: very strict ahimsa to all living beings and that truth has many sides (anekantavada).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Mahavira's idea that truth has many sides is often told through the story of people touching different parts of an elephant in the dark. What does the story teach about arguments?
prompt_hi: Mahavira ka vichaar ki sach ke kai pehlu hote hain, aksar andhere mein haathi ke alag-alag hisse chhoone wale logon ki kahani se samjhaaya jaata hai. Yeh kahani bahas ke baare mein kya sikhaati hai?
answer: Each person may know a part of the truth; listening to other views gives a fuller picture, so we should not insist only our view is right.

subject: sst
prompt_en: A student says: 'Ahimsa just means don't hit anyone. Shouting insults is fine.' What is the mistake?
prompt_hi: Ek student kehta hai: 'Ahimsa ka matlab bas kisi ko maarna nahi. Gaali dena theek hai.' Galti kya hai?
answer: Ahimsa means not causing harm in actions, words or even thoughts, to people, animals and all living beings; hurtful words also cause harm.

subject: sst
prompt_en: The Upanishads are full of questions like 'Who am I?' Why might asking questions and debating be an important part of a knowledge tradition?
prompt_hi: Upanishads mein 'Main kaun hoon?' jaise kai sawaal hain. Kisi gyaan parampara mein sawaal poochhna aur bahas karna kyon zaroori ho sakta hai?
answer: Questions and debate let people test ideas, explain them better and discover new ones; many schools of thought grew this way rather than everyone accepting one view.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Put these in order on a timeline: the Rig Veda composed; the Buddha and Mahavira teach; today. Then say roughly how long ago the Buddha lived.
prompt_hi: Inhe timeline pe order mein lagao: Rig Veda ki rachna; Buddha aur Mahavira ki shiksha; aaj. Phir batao Buddha lagbhag kitne saal pehle the.
answer: Rig Veda first, then the Buddha and Mahavira, then today; the Buddha lived about 2,500 years ago.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Name one practice in your home, town or community that shows respect for nature or for all living beings. Which idea from this chapter does it connect to?
prompt_hi: Apne ghar, sheher ya samudaay ki koi aisi parampara batao jo prakriti ya sabhi jeevon ke prati samman dikhaati ho. Yeh is chapter ke kis vichaar se judi hai?
answer: Any reasonable example (feeding birds, not cutting a sacred tree or grove, saving water, kindness to animals) linked to ahimsa or respect for nature in folk, tribal or other traditions.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Predict: if two people from different schools of thought sit down to debate respectfully, what is more likely — that both learn something, or that one must be silenced?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar alag-alag vichaardhaara ke do log izzat se bahas karein, to kya hone ki sambhavna zyada hai — dono kuch seekhenge, ya ek ko chup karana padega?
answer: Both are likely to learn something; respectful debate (shastrartha) helped Indian traditions grow and sharpen their ideas.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Explain to a friend what 'India's cultural roots' means, using the Vedas, the Buddha and Mahavira, and folk traditions as examples.
prompt_hi: Ek dost ko samjhao ki 'Bharat ki saanskritik jadein' ka kya matlab hai — Vedas, Buddha, Mahavira aur lok paramparaon ke examples ke saath.
answer: Many old knowledge traditions: the Vedas (oral, Rig Veda oldest), Upanishads with deep questions, the Buddha's Middle Path, Mahavira's ahimsa and many-sidedness, and folk/tribal respect for nature; they grew through dialogue and share values like non-harm.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Name three harvest festivals celebrated in different parts of India around mid-January.
prompt_hi: Mid-January ke aas-paas Bharat ke alag-alag hisson mein manaye jaane wale 3 fasal tyohaaron ke naam batao.
answer: Any three of: Pongal (Tamil Nadu), Bihu/Magh Bihu (Assam), Lohri (Punjab), Makar Sankranti (many states), Uttarayan (Gujarat).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why is a garland of different flowers on one thread a good picture of 'unity in diversity'?
prompt_hi: Ek dhaage mein alag-alag phoolon ki maala 'anekta mein ekta' ki achhi tasveer kyon hai?
answer: The flowers stay different (diversity) but the one thread holds them together (shared values and belonging), and together they are more beautiful than one kind alone.

subject: sst
prompt_en: The Ramayana is told as Kamba Ramayanam in Tamil and as Ramcharitmanas in Awadhi. What does this show about Indian culture?
prompt_hi: Ramayana Tamil mein Kamba Ramayanam aur Awadhi mein Ramcharitmanas ke roop mein kahi gayi. Isse Bharatiya sanskriti ke baare mein kya pata chalta hai?
answer: A shared story is retold in many languages and styles across regions — one story, many forms — showing unity with diversity.

subject: sst
prompt_en: A student writes: 'Everyone in India speaks Hindi at home.' Spot the mistake.
prompt_hi: Ek student ne likha: 'Bharat mein sab ghar pe Hindi bolte hain.' Galti pakdo.
answer: India has many languages; many people speak Tamil, Telugu, Bengali, Marathi, Kannada, Malayalam, Odia, Assamese, Punjabi, Gujarati and others at home; 22 languages are in the Eighth Schedule.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare how Pongal (Tamil Nadu) and Lohri (Punjab) are celebrated: one thing the same, one thing different.
prompt_hi: Pongal (Tamil Nadu) aur Lohri (Punjab) kaise manaye jaate hain compare karo: ek cheez jo same hai, ek jo alag.
answer: Same: both are winter harvest festivals in mid-January, giving thanks for crops. Different: Pongal is marked by cooking the sweet dish pongal from new rice (and honouring cattle); Lohri by a bonfire, with sesame, jaggery and popcorn, songs and dance.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Predict: if everyone in India had to give up their own language and food for just one, what would the country lose?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar Bharat mein sabko apni bhasha aur khana chhod kar sirf ek apnana pade, to desh kya kho dega?
answer: It would lose many stories, songs, knowledge, recipes and ways of life carried in different languages and cultures; people might also feel they no longer belong.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Many regions celebrate a harvest festival at the same time of year with different names. Why might that be?
prompt_hi: Kai ilaake saal ke ek hi samay pe alag naamon se fasal ka tyohaar manaate hain. Aisa kyon ho sakta hai?
answer: Farming follows similar seasons across much of India, so the harvest comes around the same time, and people everywhere give thanks for it in their own local way.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Make a Venn diagram (or say it in words) comparing dosa from South India and chilla from North India: what goes in each circle and in the middle?
prompt_hi: South India ke dosa aur North India ke chilla ka Venn diagram banao (ya shabdon mein batao): har circle mein kya aur beech mein kya?
answer: Middle: both are thin pancakes made by spreading a batter on a hot pan. Dosa circle: batter of rice and urad dal, usually fermented overnight. Chilla circle: batter usually of besan (gram flour) or moong dal, often not fermented.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Look around your neighbourhood or class: find two families or friends who celebrate differently. What do they share, and what is different?
prompt_hi: Apne mohalle ya class mein dekho: do parivaar ya dost dhoondo jo alag tarah se tyohaar manaate hon. Unme kya saanjha hai aur kya alag?
answer: Any real example naming at least one shared thing (food sharing, lights, family gatherings, values like care) and one difference (dates, rituals, songs, dishes, language).
